test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Fitter) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the ball is thrown upwards, then the work done by the force of gravity on the ball is:

options.text: Independent of the displacement of the ball

solution:
__**Concept:**__

Work done by a force is given by:

 W = F · d · costheta 

When a ball is thrown **upwards**:

 
• Gravity acts downward.
 
• Displacement is upward.
 
• Angle between force of gravity and displacement = 180^circ.

Thus,

 W = mgd times cos 180^circ = -mgd 

The work is **negative** because gravity acts opposite to the motion.
